biggest_gap.title: At volume, the list gate only judges one-letter searches. A tenant-blind total for broad multi-letter searches (initials path), kept on disk, passes all of G1
biggest_gap.detail: p05 promises that G1 attacks every list registered with the framework, and every later 100,000-row list relies on that. After round 9, ListVolume judges each list at demo volume. Its searches are one-letter words only: 14 letters, plus sorted and grouped versions of them. The engine runs different code for other search shapes. One word of 2 to 5 Latin letters takes the initials path (InitialsWord and InitialsMatch: an extra regular-expression condition and an initials score). A broad answer (over MaxRankedRows) also has its own branch. Neither runs at volume in any gate, and the small-volume gates never get a broad answer. The structural checks only look at process memory (ProcessState), and the process-global rule in TenantSource does not cover the file system. So a total remembered in the temp folder, keyed without the tenant, is invisible to every check. That is a natural optimisation of the slowest answer while someone types ('ma' reads the regular expression on about 30,000 rows). Plant L13 does exactly that. Fixes: (a) Build the volume query set from the engine's branches, not from letters. Include one word of each length from 2 to MaxInitials that is broad (over MaxRankedRows) in both tenants with different counts, and one that is ranked. Add multi-word searches (broad and ranked), Arabic words of 2 or more letters, and digit searches. Send each as B, A, B, A. Report 'blind' for any branch with no discriminating query, as is already done for Unranked and Ranked. (b) Give TenantSource a reviewed rule for file-system and other external state in product code: System.IO File, Directory and FileStream writes, Path.GetTempPath, MemoryMappedFile, named Mutex or Semaphore. (c) Add the L13 shape to the ListVolume self-test, next to the existing 'total memo for big filtered queries'.
biggest_gap.evidence: Apply gauntlet/evidence/p05-list-search/r12/L13-broad-initials-total-memo-on-disk.patch to ebb48972. Run the G1 suite in the toolbox image with scripts/plant-gate-run.sh <copy> L13 'FullyQualifiedName~Erp.Gates.Tests.G1': all 68 tests pass (run-L13-only-g1-all.log, EXIT 0). Then run ./erp up on the planted copy and node scripts/probe-l13.mjs http://localhost:<port> ma sa ra. Gulfsteel (1,005 users) is answered 30,568 for 'ma' after alnoor asked, while its own keyset walk returns 314 rows. 'sa' gives 14,778 against 164 and 'ra' 20,054 against 168 (plant-live-L13.txt). On screen, gulfsteel's Users list shows '30,568 users' for 'ma' (plant-L13-second-tenant-sees-first-tenants-search-count.jpg).

other_findings: Plant P10, a screen-permission miss on p05's own list component, is the same kind of fault as the G2 fail recorded under hard_gates. ListView.tsx canChange becomes 'isMine || isShared', dropping the canShare check, so a reader without lists.views.share is offered 'Update this view' and 'Delete this view' on the workspace's shared views. All 504 web unit tests pass with it. The e2e test for the reader only asserts that the save dialog has no share box. The server still refuses the write, so no data changes. Fix: the screen sweep, or a ListView unit test, should open a shared view as a reader with canShare false and assert that neither action is offered.

Plant P11 has two variants. The first, POST /views/{id}/share turning the caller's own view into a shared one in place, failed G2's list-view test and G1 HttpIsolation only by side effect: the administrator's later DELETE and B's later PUT on that view got 404 (run-L13-P11-g1-g2.log). The copy variant P11b is caught only by the reviewed list read-permission-writes.txt. The behavioural list-view check passed. It sends the reader's writes only to POST /views and PUT /views/{id}, and never sends a POST route with an id carrying the reader's own view id. G2's derived permission rule also accepts any route under /api/lists/{key}/ that does not start with 'shared-views' as correctly guarded by the list's read permission, without review. If a reviewer accepted a read-permission-writes line ('a reader shares their own view'), nothing behavioural would catch it. Fix: send every write route under /api/lists/{key}/ (any method, any shape) as a reader without share, using the reader's own view ids, then assert that no shared view appears or changes.

[route: p00-foundation] The process-global rule of the G1 tenant-source scanner (G1TenantSourceTests.cs) and ProcessState cover in-process stores only: AppContext, pools, caches, thread-static. State kept on the file system (temp files, MemoryMappedFile, named synchronisation objects) by any module escapes both. L13 used Path.GetTempPath and File.WriteAllText and was not flagged.

G3 processor time: both clean-clone verifies had every test green (1,687) but exceeded verify.cpuSeconds: 10,996 s with my plant G1 run beside it, and 11,212 s from my clone alone while other agents kept the load up to 79. The integration verify of b9afbfd6 recorded 10,092 s. No maximum was changed. A quieter re-run is needed to tell whether this is load or growth.

Scope in the browser at 1600x900 over 100,005 users (ui-scope.txt). The list renders in 123 ms with 32 DOM rows, and the search box has the focus on arrival. Typing 'khalid haddad' as you type gives 57 matches in about 290 ms, and Enter opens the best match in the details panel. ArrowDown enters the grid. End reaches row 100,006 in about 1.5 s with 32 DOM rows (virtualised), and Home goes back. Space and Shift+Arrow select and offer Copy, Deactivate and Activate. Enter on the Name header sorts ascending. The column menu offers sort, Filter… and Hide this column. Grouping by language shows Arabic 20,163 and English 79,842. The column chooser reorders columns. In Arabic the page is dir=rtl with Arabic headers and '100,005 مستخدمين', and 'محمد السويدى' (ى variant) finds 107 matches with 'محمد السويدي' first. Server time over 100,005 users (perf.txt): every query has a median under 225 ms.
